subsections.subsection_title: 66. EXAMINER VIVA — VAGINAL EXAMINATION AND PROM

blocks.text: “Should you perform repeated digital vaginal examinations in PPROM?”

No. Avoid unnecessary digital examinations because of infection risk. Use a sterile speculum when assessment of membrane rupture is required and perform digital examination only when clinically necessary.

“I would explain the procedure, obtain consent, offer a chaperone, ensure privacy and position the patient comfortably. I would inspect externally for bleeding, liquor or cord prolapse and then gently perform a vaginal examination. I would assess the cervix for dilatation, effacement, consistency and position. I would identify the presenting part and determine the fetal position, then assess station and descent. I would assess whether the membranes are intact and, if ruptured, the liquor. Finally, I would assess for caput and moulding. I would correlate the findings with previous examinations to determine progress and assess whether there is evidence of malposition, obstruction or fetal compromise. I would report and document the findings clearly.”
**A vaginal examination is not just “how many centimetres?”**
And the most important safety principle:
**Never interpret one vaginal examination in isolation. Compare with previous findings to determine whether labour is progressing.**
